findings.text: Early boot offers two IDT services, one that prepares APIC entries plus generic external and spurious gates then maps and reloads the table and freezes it read only, and one that installs a single system vector handler during the setup window.

IDT construction moves from table driven APIC gate creation through filling unclaimed external vectors with shared IRQ stubs and unclaimed system vectors with spurious stubs where supported, then mapping into the CPU entry area and reloading and write protecting and latching a done flag that blocks later installs.

System vector installation rejects numbers below the system range and any attempt after setup completion, and claims each vector atomically so a second install of the same number does not overwrite the gate.
IO delay selector values are 0 for the 0x80 port variant and 1 for the 0xED port variant and 2 for the microsecond delay variant and 3 for the no delay variant.
Build configuration selects exactly one of the four delay selectors as the initial value of the global delay type held in mostly read memory.

Runtime exposes a delay routine dispatching on the global selector and an early init routine consulting firmware identity unless overridden and a boot parameter handler accepting four textual names to force the selector and latch override.

Delay selection starts at the configured default and may move from the 0x80 choice to the 0xED choice on matched firmware and moves to any explicitly requested choice when the boot parameter is present, after which firmware matching is skipped.

Firmware matching consults a short constant table with five entries sharing one callback and one board vendor plus distinct board names and terminated by an empty entry, where the callback only changes state when the current selector is the 0x80 variant and always reports success.

Boot parameter parsing rejects missing or unrecognized delay names with an invalid argument error and otherwise records the chosen selector and latches the override flag to block later firmware changes.

Per thread IO permission state combines an emulation level plus an optional refcounted bitmap object holding a full port bitmap and a refcount and a cached byte length of the significant prefix and a sequence number, with a global 64 bit counter supplying fresh sequence values.

Permission range updates reject wrap around and ranges beyond the bitmap size and require raw IO privilege and an unlocked IO port lockdown state when enabling, while clearing without an existing bitmap succeeds without allocation and first enable lazily allocates a fully denied bitmap.

Bitmap ownership starts absent and is allocated on first enable and is shared across fork by incrementing the refcount and flagging the child and is duplicated on write when shared, with hardware refresh deferred to return to user mode through flag and sequence bump and release when permissions become empty or the thread exits.
User mode reaches permission control through port range and privilege level system calls, where one build provides full logic and an alternate build reports unimplemented for both calls.

Privilege level updates accept only levels zero through three and return immediately when unchanged and demand raw IO privilege and unlocked state when raising the level, then store the new emulated level and refresh bitmap state.

Bitmap deactivation clears the thread flag then updates the hardware task state with preemption disabled, while activation and permission edits only set the flag and sequence because the hardware update is deferred to exit to user mode.

Interrupt vector to descriptor lookup runs lock free on the fast path and acquires the global vector lock only when reevaluating a missing or shutdown entry to close a race with concurrent setup and teardown.

Interrupt statistics metadata is a fixed array indexed by counter identifier, where each record carries an optional vector used for display suppression plus a short symbol and a longer human readable label, built with helpers for plain and vector tagged and always suppressed rows.

At init each statistics row is shown when it has no suppression vector or when its vector is reserved in the system set, with later clearing of platform and notification and deferred error rows when the corresponding callback or feature or CPU vendor is unavailable.

Architecture code exposes helpers to render enabled counters with per CPU breakdowns into sequential output and to sum all counters for a given CPU, plus a bad IRQ acknowledgment that logs under rate limit and always signals end of interrupt.

External interrupts enter through a common gate that tracks IRQ registers and RCU state and dispatches through per CPU descriptor lookup and signals completion when no handler exists, with 32 bit handling able to redirect to a dedicated IRQ stack unless already there or in user mode.

Low stack in interrupt context triggers a warning and diagnostic dump with optional panic, and an overflow report can be issued from the IRQ stack, while reentrant interrupts detected by comparing current and per CPU stack bases stay on the current stack to avoid corruption.

Per CPU vector slots distinguish valid descriptors from unused and shutdown markers, logging a rate limited emergency message for the unused case and normalizing shutdown to unused under lock before reporting absence.

System vectors provide dedicated handlers for platform IPIs with optional callback and tracing and for guest mediated performance interrupts and for three KVM posted interrupt flavors including a wakeup indirection and for a posted MSI notification drain.

Posted interrupt wakeup uses a function pointer defaulting to a no operation routine and replaceable at runtime, with reclamation synchronization when reset to the default and preservation of the prior handler when given an empty update.

Posted MSI notification drains pending virtual vectors in a bounded loop and rearms by clearing the outstanding flag then drains once more to cover a race, while acknowledgment moves the IRQ and only signals completion directly when the posted handler is not active.
Posted MSI coalescing bound is 3 and statistics suppression sentinel equals UINT_MAX.

Unexpected vectors mainly on multiprocessor APIC systems must still be acknowledged to avoid occupying priority slots and stalling lower priority delivery, and retriggered posted MSI vectors need explicit completion to avoid stale in service state.
IRQ core instantiates trace points once and generic descriptor dispatch selects 64 bit direct handling versus 32 bit stack aware handling at build time.
